differences.ink: An upright stem and top, middle and bottom strokes coexist with a rounded contour. Plain E is my first candidate; the superposed contour is not a securely separate displaced second E impression. The other candidates remain visually possible. The right-hand F is a clean, different, single glyph.

differences.ink: Both R letters are ordinary single serifed capitals. The left m and f have separate primes; the right m and f do not. Both exponent endings are minus one. The lower signs have intersecting pen strokes consistent with stars.
differences.math_consequence: Confirms written degrees m'-1 and m-1; no proof of the map.

differences.ink: The second letter has a short upright and upper-right shoulder of r, not the closed contour of e. The u and x are clear.

The 2 has the same curved shoulder, descending oblique and flat foot as the typed-looking 2 in both following 2n exponents. I prefer typewriter provenance; the number itself is certain. Pen versus type is not conclusively separable from the reproduction.
differences.math_consequence: The degree is certainly 2; only the source layer differs.

differences.ink: Single Z with a separate lower rule extending toward/through the adjoining crossed glyph. The subscript has an upper-left hook, oblique descending stroke and horizontal foot, matching D03/D04. A looped pen ell is not secure; chi is the closest literal candidate. H's bold Z is unsupported.
differences.math_consequence: The coefficient parameter remains a literal alphabet uncertainty.

differences.ink: Final i is followed by the word space before par; no final e.
Serifed typewriter lowercase x at the baseline and lowered S, rather than a centered diagonal multiplication cross.
Ordinary single H. Exponent 2 followed by clear n without a descender.
Single typed Z, independent lower rule, and the same mechanical crossed subscript with hook and flat foot. Chi follows the first occurrence's marked ambiguity, without a separate semantic claim.
differences.math_consequence: Recurring alphabet uncertainty is marked at D02.

differences.ink: The inline product uses the same baseline serifed x and lowered S as D03.

At t a full rounded lower contour survives around the tall t stem and crossbar: more than a heavy single t. An old o is provisionally recorded under the live t. The old letter is unsure because its full contour and superposition order are not secured.
Between clear i and following m is an extra typewriter cell with crossing x strokes and rounded/crossbar remnants. Old e is closest, not absorbed into m. The live word remains vraiment.
At the v cell an ascender with left top serif and lower rounded bowl survives beneath the v diagonals. Old b is closest, marked unsure; no entire earlier word is restored.
null- is clear; a small left curved fragment of the next glyph survives at the cut edge. The full final e cannot be read.
differences.math_consequence: Characteristic-zero wording probable; final letter clipped.

differences.ink: The first glyph has d's upright ascender and lower rounded part, followed by y. The later cycle on the line has a normal c for comparison.
Two upright typed quotation strokes on each side; no angled guillemets.

notes: The page continues a correspondence-induced map of higher direct images in degrees m'-1 and m-1 and says it yields a map on H^1(S, ). The first coefficient remains undecided by the clear target F_Y.

Y' becomes a relative curve C, m'=2, and x' is the degree-2 class of t_1(S)-t_0(S). The page asserts primitivity for geometrically connected fibres and allows any relative divisor of relative degree zero. Reading is not proof of that cohomological assertion.

Z is written in degree 2n on Y x_S C with twist (n), associated to a codimension-n cycle. x has the same degree/twist on Y and corresponds to z = Z(t_1)-Z(t_0). Minus and 1/0 indices were read directly.

The author says 'pour que cette classe de cohomologie soit vraiment définie en l'état actuel de la Science, il faut faire des hypothèses restrictives'. Visible old letter remnants in notera, vraiment and restrictives are retained.

The alternatives concern S of finite type over a field, S excellent of characteristic nulle (clipped), or the 'dycle' Z a 'relatif' cycle of codimension less than or equal to n fibre by fibre. The source inequality is not changed for expected mathematics.
The final NB says 'on suppose que les intersections écrites ont un sens' and refers to underlined classes of cycles. Both outer NB closures are absent in the readable ink.
The mechanical-looking chi/ell glyph is not forced to a mathematical prime parameter; the frozen table is only comparative.
No other page image, reader output, OCR, web source, published text or external theorem was consulted.

check_events.outcome: Conditional arithmetic calculation only, with no formal certificate: assuming each section divisor restricts to degree 1 on a geometric fibre, deg(t_1(s)-t_0(s))=1-1=0. This checks that arithmetic feature only. It does not prove cohomological primitivity, the cycle-class construction, or the correspondence action.

non_text_observations.observation: Two isolated strokes inspected in restriction_edge_inequality crop; interpretation open. No authorial letter, parenthesis or drawing inferred.
Faint vertical/edge traces apart from clearly separate pencil 10 treated as paper/scan background.

brief_feedback: The v02 rules were sufficient. A future brief could state an explicit convention for hand-drawn underlining of typed letters and uncertain pen/type provenance. Here \handwritten{\uline}{classes} marks only the underline command; typed letters stay outside. Single old glyphs are retained as \deleted{\unsure{...}} instead of restoring whole prior words. Isolated edge traces are documented without inventing a parenthesis or drawing.
